name: Postsecondary Planning for Students With Disabilities
title: Postsecondary Planning for Students With Disabilities
answer: Postsecondary planning for students with disabilities means connecting their transition plans to goals after high school and preparing them for a different accommodations system. Colleges and employers generally handle accommodations differently from schools, and students usually have to request them on their own. This matters because a student's ability to explain their needs and ask for support becomes central to success after high school.

sections.body: Students with disabilities have extra planning needs because their transition plans should align with what they want to do after high school. In college and at work, accommodations are not arranged the same way as in a school setting, and students are usually responsible for requesting them. Counselors and special education staff can help students understand this shift and get ready for it. AI can support the research by helping students look into disability services at colleges and training programs. The student and their support team then go over what the tool found and decide what to do next.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: The supplied text does not give grade bands for this idea, so the practice applies across secondary planning. A student might use AI to compare what documentation different colleges require or what supports they offer. The student and their support team review the findings and plan next steps. Self advocacy is the most important skill to build, so students can practice describing their needs and requesting accommodations. Mock conversations with a school configured tool, followed by discussion with a counselor, can help the student become someone who can advocate for their own needs.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The supplied text gives no evidence label, study, figure, or finding for this idea. It rests on practice rather than research. The guidance is presented as practical planning advice for counselors, special education staff, and students.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The disability services office at each college should be treated as the final authority for official information, so AI research does not replace that source. The student and their support team review findings and plan next steps, which keeps decisions with people rather than the tool. Colleges and employers provide accommodations differently than schools, and students must usually request them on their own, so preparation cannot remove that responsibility. Mock conversations with a school configured tool are followed by discussion with a counselor, not left as the only support. The goal is a student who can advocate for their own needs, which means the student remains the person who describes their needs and asks for accommodations.
